text: Artificial intelligence systems learn useful representations from data. A language model learns statistical relationships between tokens and uses those relationships to predict future tokens.
Machine learning uses data to construct models that discover patterns. Training minimizes an objective function and optimization changes model parameters according to observed error.
Deep learning uses layered neural networks. Each layer transforms representations and produces features that are useful for later computations.
Transformer models use attention to route information between sequence positions. Queries, keys, and values determine how representations interact.
Autoregressive language modeling predicts the next token from previous tokens. The training target is shifted by one position relative to the model input.
Silverwing is designed as a personal artificial intelligence architecture containing memory, reasoning, tools, learning systems, evaluation, and controlled adaptation.
Persistent memory allows a system to retain useful information beyond one execution. Semantic retrieval helps select relevant information for future tasks.
An intelligent agent receives goals, chooses actions, observes results, evaluates outcomes, and continues until the task reaches a useful completion state.
Reliable artificial intelligence requires monitoring, error handling, validation, observability, recovery, and controlled deployment of new versions.
Scientific learning requires observations, hypotheses, measurements, experiments, analysis, replication, and revision when evidence contradicts previous assumptions.
Biological systems continuously interact with their environments. Adaptation changes system behavior in response to internal and external conditions.
Physical systems are described using quantities, relationships, conservation laws, and models that explain measurable behavior.
Continual learning requires mechanisms for receiving new information, evaluating it, updating representations, and preventing damaging changes to previously learned skills.

Controlled self improvement should produce a candidate change, run an experiment, measure the result, compare it against the previous version, and promote the candidate only when evaluation criteria are satisfied.
Engineering systems should be modular, testable, observable, reproducible, and recoverable. Components should communicate through well-defined interfaces.
